one_liner: Civil litigator for DOJ in DC who investigates and sues companies and individuals under the False Claims Act to recover money for the government.
fit_summary: This attorney-only job requires a J.D., active bar membership and at least three years of post-J.D. experience. Daniel's degree is an M.A. in Global Affairs, so he cannot qualify.
eligibility: Active bar membership in good standing in any U.S. jurisdiction is required.
Minimum three years of post-J.D. legal or other relevant experience, met by the closing date; significant litigation experience is preferred.
U.S. citizenship and a Top Secret clearance are required; the posting is open to the public and does not require federal status.
You must reside in DC or within 25 miles of it (28 U.S.C. 545).
strategy: Look at the same office and at agency Offices of Inspector General for non-attorney roles that support fraud work, such as paralegal specialist (0950), investigator (1801/1810), or grants and program analyst positions.
FEMA grant compliance roles are another option that builds on his work helping counties update COVID-19 emergency grant applications.
interview_questions: Walk us through how you would evaluate a new qui tam complaint alleging grant fraud.
Describe your litigation experience, including depositions, discovery, and trial work.
How do you manage multiple investigations at once while meeting court deadlines?
Tell us about a time you worked with law enforcement or a whistleblower to build a case.
watch_outs: Hard requirements: a J.D., active bar membership and three or more years of legal experience, none of which he has.
A Top Secret clearance is required, which means a lengthy background investigation.
